extra_misconceptions.fact: Cross-ventilation using two openings and an exhaust fan is required to keep solvent vapors below toxic and flammable thresholds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Opening a single window provides enough airflow to safely apply solvent-based primers indoors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paper masks filter only solid particles; chemical strippers require an organic vapor respirator and chemical-resistant gloves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A standard paper dust mask blocks toxic organic vapors released by chemical paint strippers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Metal scrapers can nick live insulation and spark flammable fumes, so nearby circuits must be shut off or shielded before prep work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scraping loose paint near a plugged-in extension cord poses no hazard as long as the cord is dry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pigmented wood stain adds color inside the wood pores but offers minimal abrasion or moisture resistance unless sealed with varnish.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Interior wood stain seals and protects bare oak furniture from water rings without a clear topcoat.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Alkyd resins cure by solvent evaporation followed by chemical cross-linking with oxygen, creating a harder and slower-drying film.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Oil-based alkyd paints dry solely through water evaporation in the same way as latex wall paints.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-traffic trim and wet rooms need satin, semi-gloss, or gloss enamel because tighter resin films resist scrubbing and moisture.

extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pure 100 percent silicone caulk holds latex trim paint tightly around window casings and baseboards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Porous drywall patch absorbs binder from unprimed topcoats, leaving dull flat spots known as flashing that remain visible after drying.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying two thick coats of wall paint eliminates the need to spot-prime patched drywall compound.

extra_misconceptions.fact: New concrete must cure for at least 28 days and pass a plastic-sheet moisture test so trapped alkalinity and vapor do not blister paint.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Complementary colors sit directly opposite each other on the color wheel, while adjacent hues form an analogous color harmony.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Complementary colors sit directly next to each other on the standard twelve-part artist color wheel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Equal areas of full-strength complements create jarring visual vibration; one color should dominate while the opposite serves as an accent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mixing equal surface areas of two intense complementary colors produces a calm, low-contrast room scheme.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Adding white lightens a hue into a pastel tint, whereas mixing black or a complementary color darkens the hue into a shade or tone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding white paint to darken a primary blue creates a deep shade suitable for trim accents.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Light source color temperature shifts how pigments reflect wavelengths, so swatches must be tested under the project's actual lighting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Paint chips viewed under cool fluorescent store lights look identical under warm incandescent bulbs at home.

extra_misconceptions.misconception: Natural hog-bristle brushes are ideal for spreading water-based acrylic latex wall and trim paints.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Resting weight on wet bristles bends them permanently; cleaned brushes must hang by the handle hole or lie flat in their keeper sleeve.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing a washed paintbrush upright on its bristles in a bucket preserves the chiseled tip shape.

extra_misconceptions.misconception: Warm tap water and dish soap dissolve cured oil-based enamel from roller covers and synthetic brushes.
